name: SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings
problem: Supervised sentence-embedding methods needed a separately trained model per dataset, so embeddings did not transfer.
mechanism: Unsupervised variant: drop the same sentence into the encoder twice and predict one from the other under a contrastive objective, using ONLY STANDARD DROPOUT as the noise source. Supervised variant: use NLI entailment pairs as positives and contradiction pairs as hard negatives. Also shows the objective regularises the pretrained embedding space away from anisotropy.
speedup_reported: Unsupervised and supervised BERT-base models average 76.3% and 81.6% Spearman correlation on standard STS tasks, improvements of 4.2% and 2.2% over the previous best results. This is a quality delta on STS benchmarks, not a cost or latency measurement.
notes: Venue EMNLP 2021 (crossref ACL proceedings; arXiv comment 'Accepted to EMNLP 2021'). Inference cost is identical to SBERT with the same base model - the contribution is entirely in the training objective, which is worth stating plainly because SimCSE is sometimes misread as an architecture change. It is a drop-in quality upgrade to an already-deployed encoder at zero serving cost.
